statement: Broadcom management said land, power and shell availability dictate the timing of AI capacity deployment, alongside substrate, HBM and leading-edge wafer constraints.
why: When the binding constraint moves from silicon to buildings and electricity, chip orders can outrun what can actually be switched on.

impact.mechanism: Physical site, power and upstream component lead times gate how quickly accelerators can be installed, stretching the delay between order and deployed capacity.

evidence.excerpt: Land, power, and shell, as I indicated to a question with Will, is a big concern...More than a big concern, it dictates specific timing of when this capacity gets deployed.

confidence.basis: Verbatim management remark but read via secondary transcript coverage; no lead-time figures were quantified.

dispersion: CEO also said supply is secured for fiscal 2027/2028 targets while demand runs ahead of the outlook.
